links.comparator_used: Same clinical scenarios under neutral and six Milgram-style social-pressure conditions without the brief mitigation cue ('verify or escalate if unsafe')
links.effect: Mitigation reduced harmful decisions from 16.6% to 10.1% (p < 0.001); under pressure conditions harmful output was mitigated 8.3–9.6% vs unmitigated 14.3–16.0%
links.tradeoff: Mitigation did not eliminate harm: about 10% of responses remained potentially harmful, and authority or responsibility-transfer pressure still produced the most harmful responses. No cost or latency data were reported.
links.quote: Mitigation reduced harmful decisions from 16.6% to 10.1% (p < 0.001).
